source.sequence: Phonemic awareness moves from larger spoken parts to single sounds, then to changing a sound. The order is word awareness, rhyme, syllables, onset-rime, then one level per phoneme: simple consonants, short vowels, consonant digraphs, two-letter blends, three-letter blends, vowel teams and diphthongs, and r-controlled vowels. Phoneme deletion and substitution stays last. Each phoneme level asks the child to isolate the target, blend the word, and segment it into Elkonin boxes. A blend is two or three separate phonemes. A digraph is one phoneme. Marilyn Jager Adams, Beginning to Read (1990); National Reading Panel (2000); Liberman, Shankweiler, Fischer, and Carter (1974); D. B. Elkonin (1973); Ehri and others in the National Reading Panel phonemic awareness report (2001); David A. Kilpatrick, Equipped for Reading Success (2015). Older struggling readers are included. Kilpatrick treats phoneme deletion and substitution as the skill that still needs work for many of them.
source.audio: The computer speaks the say field. The child answers out loud. Nothing on the screen has to be read. A correct answer is silent, then the next item after advanceMs. A wrong answer, or no answer for maxShowMs, speaks the model field, waits advanceMs, and then goes to the next item. The microphone listens only while that item is waiting for an answer. Nothing is recorded or saved.
source.movement: riseAfter correct answers in a row move up one band. One miss stays on the band. dropAfter misses in a row move down one band. The first band does not move down. The last band does not move up. The student's grade number stays as it was sent.

placement.note: Age 4 starts at word awareness (Pre-K). Age 5 starts at rhyme (K). Those ages win over the grade, because the grade form starts at 1st. Grade 1 starts at the first consonant level. Grade 2 starts at phoneme deletion and substitution. Grade 3 and above starts at that same grade 2 band, so an older struggling reader can use the engine and can be moved down. A saved band is kept. Saved bands IS, BL, and PS from the earlier list map to the first consonant level, the first two-letter blend level, and the first vowel-team level.
